history.rationale: The arginine-rich motif (positions 49-57) is essential for Tat transactivation; conservative R-to-K substitution preserves positive charge and DNA-binding capability while maintaining protein viability.
Solid evolutionary tolerance (0.0204) and neutral-to-positive plm score; retains viability signal while aligning with ARM region conservation.
Highest toxicity score (0.585) indicates likely impaired function, warranting downgrade
Position 50 lies within the core basic domain critical for TAR RNA interaction; swapping to arginine maintains electrostatic properties and is a common tolerated change in Tat homologs.
High toxicity (0.54) reduces suitability for replication optimization
K51 is part of the RKKR cluster; R-for-K substitution keeps the motif highly basic, likely preserving or slightly enhancing transactivation without disrupting overall Tat folding.
Elevated toxicity (0.4) conflicts with viability priority
Arginine at 52 directly contacts RNA; R-to-K change retains charge and is frequently observed in functional Tat variants, supporting improved replication efficiency.
Moderate toxicity (0.42) conflicts with top-tier prior, requiring downgrade
R53 contributes to the arginine-rich activation domain; conservative substitution to lysine maintains viability and can enhance transactivation by optimizing charge distribution.
Highest mutant frequency in homologs (0.0638) and sequence-plm plausibility (0.0427) among all candidates; both tools show strong local support for this substitution in the basic domain.
ToxinPred3 score of 0.38 meets toxicity threshold, conflicting with viability requirement despite high prior confidence
Q54 is a non-basic residue in the motif; R-for-Q change introduces an additional positive charge, potentially strengthening TAR binding while remaining conservative enough to preserve function.
Low toxicity (0.36) supports reranking above higher-toxin alternatives
R55 is a key contact residue in the basic domain; R-to-K substitution preserves charge and is a standard tolerated mutation that can improve Tat-mediated transactivation.
Moderate-to-good MSA frequency (0.0233) and plm support; position is functionally relevant in transactivation motif without major red flags.
Lowest toxicity (0.28) strongly supports improved viability while retaining solid prior
R56 participates in the RRRQRRR cluster; conservative R-to-K change maintains the highly basic character required for efficient virus replication via enhanced transactivation.
Very low toxicity (0.23) combined with strong prior makes it top candidate
C-terminal R57 of the arginine-rich motif is critical for function; R-to-K substitution keeps positive charge and is commonly accepted, likely boosting transactivation without compromising viability.
Lowest toxicity (0.23) elevates it above others with comparable priors
